### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 42 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `78ac70748fed2ec9853aabb65ce179fd9adb3a7f` — the merge of head `1a4eb0cf80a72df05c8bde66858344a65de3ceda` into base `b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 78ac70748fed2ec9853aabb65ce179fd9adb3a7f && git checkout 78ac70748fed2ec9853aabb65ce179fd9adb3a7f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91 1a4eb0cf80a72df05c8bde66858344a65de3ceda && git checkout -B drift-repro b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91 && git merge --no-ff 1a4eb0cf80a72df05c8bde66858344a65de3ceda

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b6e870707b95d7b8ee9cedd68ad358b51de0da91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1a4eb0cf80a72df05c8bde66858344a65de3ceda`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/*.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.user-field-foreign-reference-refused.ts, packages/lint/src/** (withdrawn advisory) + .changeset/24952-user-field-reference-refused.md

### ① Derived judgments

- The refusal sits in `FieldSchema`'s superRefine (`field.zod.ts:2441-2475`), the single schema every field door composes: `ObjectSchema` and `ObjectExtensionSchema` through the shared field map, `defineStack` objects, and the metadata save door (`kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts:91`).
- No false positive: an absent `reference`, `''` and `'sys_user'` all parse, and no other user-object alias exists (`field-value.zod.ts:179-181`).
- Stored data survives:
  - the boot-time `Registry.validate` parse (`objectql/src/registry.ts:5294`) is a logged diagnostic, not a gate (`:5107-5124`);
  - rehydration does not parse (`database-loader.ts:884`).
  
  So a stored foreign-reference `user` field still boots and serves. Its next save is refused, with the issue located at the field. `referenceTargetOf` now resolves it to `sys_user`, a runtime change the changeset FROM/TO and the D3 acceptance criteria both declare.
- The withdrawn lint advisory never shipped: there is no CHANGELOG hit, `git tag --contains e7befa7700` is empty, and both packages are at `18.0.0`. Deleting its pending note is therefore right.
- No shipped producer authors the shape. The tests are real: the base pins that accepted the shape now assert the opposite.

- **Round 2 (`1a4eb0cf80`).** `origin/main` is merged in. File by file, the PR's diff against its merge base is unchanged from the reviewed head `bf738d1f99` in every `packages/spec/src` and `packages/lint/src` file. Only `.changeset/24952-*.md` differs, and the 24808 deletion is gone. Spec 21471 tests and `test:repo` 1247 passed; lint 7069 passed.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `minor` with the BREAKING banner and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The ADR-0087 disposition is `registered` on the new D3 entry `user-field-foreign-reference-refused`. That is the right arm, because no lossless conversion exists: re-targeting a foreign `reference` to `sys_user` would resolve another object's ids against `sys_user`, and a rewrite to `lookup` adds the referential delete walk. `@objectstack/lint` has no net change against `18.0.0`, so no lint changeset is owed. `Field.user`'s only public type change is the intended narrowing of `reference` to `'sys_user'`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Landing (round 2, route B):** the pending note `.changeset/24808-user-field-foreign-reference-warning.md` is now restored byte-identical to `main` (blob `5e599bf573`), so `check-empty-changeset` is green. This PR's own changeset names `@objectstack/lint` beside `@objectstack/spec`, carries `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, and has a Supersedes paragraph that withdraws the advisory, the export and the `os explain` entry 24808 announced. Both entries land in lint's CHANGELOG. In the lockstep fixed group, naming lint moves no version.
- **Cross-repo follow-up:** objectui's `userCell` gates by the authored `reference` (`packages/fields/src/__tests__/userCell.readGate-10535.test.tsx:154-164` at pin `cf153eb2e5`). This is not a pin-gate hazard, because objectui parses neither schema, but the follow-up is filed as objectstack-ai/objectui#13305.
- **Optional:** there is no `refused-shapes.ts` detector for `os migrate meta --stored`, matching the repo norm.
- The form-field component props (`ui/component.zod.ts:6723-6743`) are a widget-prop surface outside this card.
- No governed path. `content/docs/releases/` is untouched.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24952-user-field-reference-refused`
Reviewed-by: `session_01D6F9axfoPzR7t8G1J7Ytzz`
